_comment: AS.7 + DU.2, revised 2026-09-29 (DU.3). A coordinator READS the record and ASKS for judgement. It reads calendar, mail METADATA, the news list, Ledger and the shared Assistant Context directly, because those are free, deterministic and linkable; it asks another assistant's thread only for what the record cannot say. It still has NO grant over anyone else's subject: Ledger is read-only here, it cannot browse, cannot draft or send mail, and adds to the calendar only by proposing a card a human approves. What DU.2 added stays: its own output — the daily report and that report read aloud.
blurb: Asks the other assistants what matters today and gives you one list.
_whyPublishIsGranted: Granted but classed dangerous in portal/capabilities.json, so it stops for approval every time. audiocast.create ALREADY delivers the audio to the user's iPhone through CloudKit - publishing is only for a subscribable RSS feed, which puts a file on the open internet under their name. That is the user's call each morning, not the assistant's.
_whyALongerRelayTimeout: Measured 2026-09-17. The flat 120s relay timeout is structurally too short for this assistant: its turn CONTAINS relayed turns, and each of those is itself allowed 120s. Asked to run a Daily Update, it was still waiting on the first of three handoffs when its caller gave up - so it could never report success no matter how well it worked. A coordinator's budget has to exceed the sum of what it waits on. Capped at 600s by AssistantRelay.maxTurnTimeout so content cannot hang a caller indefinitely.
_whyPinnedToClaude: 2026-09-17. Left null, the resolver picked codex, which was out of credits until Sep 19 - and it could not have known, because backendAvailability() reads the content invocation mappings, not the health probe. So a coordinator run failed for a reason nothing in the selection path could see. Pinned to claude, which probes GREEN. Set back to null once backend selection consults health; this is a workaround for that gap, not a preference about which CLI is better.
_whyItReadsTheRecord: 2026-09-29. 'Ask, don't gather' produced an Update from three relayed turns, two of which were refused for budget (AssistantRelay compared lifetime spend with the daily cap — fixed in the same change) while the user's social-media work sat in Ledger ('Post Queue', 'Posting Tracker') and in a Personal Assistant thread the relay could not address. The personalisation the old ainews rationale protected is kept by reading the subjects the Reading assistant recorded in the shared context.
_whyNoCalendarAddEvent: calendar.addEvent runs only from the approval executor with a human-approved proposal; proposeEvent is the whole of this assistant's calendar write.
_whyTheseWereAdded2026_09_29: AS.3 grants began to be ENFORCED for Workbench sessions on 2026-09-29. Before turning that on, every verb this assistant had actually called (Claude and Codex transcripts) was checked against this list; todo.addTask, audiocast.listProjects and aiweb.listAgents were in real use and are granted so enforcement breaks nothing. mail.summarize is the quarantined, local-model summary: the body never reaches this assistant.
_whyItCanReadAIJobs: Phase KN (2026-09-29). mail.summarize now reports which model made a summary and links the job's card. aijobs.* is READ-ONLY: the coordinator can see what this Mac can run and link the card; only the user changes the model.
_whyItCanPublishTheDailyUpdate: 2026-10-02. The Daily Update leads For You (owner's choice over the Assistant's own 8 AM brief). publishDailyUpdate writes ONE Assistant brief record - the Update's focus items and what changed, cut from its AI Write document - which the Assistant's iCloud record carries to the iPhone. It sends nothing outside the app. The morning job calls it after every run, so the coordinator does not have to.
